claim_support.claim: The incident narrative describes a realized serious harm (patient lost consciousness requiring emergency resuscitation) due to an unflagged ventricular tachycardia episode where device-side confidence logs were not retained.

This constitutes a failure in data retention and traceability, directly impacting patient safety monitoring capabilities under FDA QMSR 21 CFR § 820.45 (labeling/packaging controls including UDI/data integrity) and ISO 13485 Clause 7.5.9.1 (Traceability).
The lack of retained logs prevents root cause analysis, violating the requirement to document procedures for traceability in accordance with part 821.

Under EU MDR Article 83(1)-(2), manufacturers must actively gather and analyze relevant data on safety throughout the device's lifetime; missing critical event logs constitutes a failure of this post-market surveillance system.
The severity is elevated because harm was realized (Severity 4 rubric: 'realized serious harm').
Immediate field action or recall may be required if similar failures are widespread, though CAPA investigation is also necessary to determine scope.
